summary.oneLiner: GMDC is transitioning from a regional lignite miner to a national-scale critical minerals player, with Odisha coal and Copper Project Ambaji as key growth drivers; volume growth is delayed but long-term capacity expansion remains intact, with 15MTPA lignite and 15MTPA coal targets by 2035.

one-line thesis: GMDC is transitioning from a regional lignite miner to a national-scale critical minerals player, with Odisha coal and Copper Project Ambaji as key growth drivers; volume growth is delayed but long-term capacity expansion remains intact, with 15MTPA lignite and 15MTPA coal targets by 2035.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +17-20% YoY (FY25); EBITDA/margin: Stable at ~25% (lignite), power loss offset by mining gains; PAT (rptd): +15% YoY; PAT (normalized): +18% YoY (ex-one-off power CAPEX); Order book: N/A (no contract-based orders); Net debt: Zero currently, debt expected by FY27 end
guidance: Revenue growth: 10-15% FY26 (lignite), +50%+ from coal/copper by FY27; Margin: Lignite margins stable at ~25%, coal margins lower but volume-driven; Order inflow: None; Capex/commissioning: FY26-27: Rs. 2,000-2,500cr/year; Baitarani West coal mine groundbreaking in FY25, first production FY26; Copper project commissioning FY28
segment / subsidiary detail: Lignite: 8MTPA FY25 (down from 10MTPA target); 10-15% growth FY26 from 4 existing mines; New mines (Lakhpat, Walia, Damlai) to contribute from FY27; Coal: Baitarani West (15MTPA) to break ground in FY25, first production ~1MTPA in FY26, ramp to 5MTPA by FY28; Copper: Ambaji underground mine, first production FY28; Rare Earths: LOI received, commercialization in 2-3 years; Bauxite: 5MTPA, contributing Rs. 80-100cr revenue; Power: ATPS plant delayed due to spares, new PPA signed with 30paise/kWh price increase, pass-through for Rs. 300-400cr CAPEX
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of Baitarani West beyond 15MTPA to 22.5MTPA; Underground coal gasification at Burapahar for blue hydrogen; Rare earths export potential; Lignite sales beyond Gujarat; Copper concentrate sales to domestic magnet makers
margins & cost dynamics: Lignite EBITDA: Rs. 800-890/ton; Coal: Lower margins than lignite but higher volumes; Copper: Not yet modeled; Power: Negative EBITDA currently, turning positive post-PPA and CAPEX pass-through; Cost structure dominated by land acquisition and R&R (46%+ of CAPEX), not operational costs
capex / expansion: Rs. 13,000cr total through 2030; FY25: Rs. 644cr (below planned Rs. 3,000cr); FY26-27: Rs. 2,000-2,500cr/year; 46% land, 15% R&R, 30% plant/machinery; CAPEX concentrated in FY26-27 due to delayed clearances; Rs. 4,000cr for coal, Rs. 3,000cr for lignite, Rs. 3,000-4,000cr for critical minerals
capital allocation: Dividend payout: 50% of PAT; CAPEX funded by Rs. 2,000cr reserves + state-backed credit line; Debt expected from FY27 end; No equity dilution planned; Focus on internal accruals and state financing
risks & watch-items: Land acquisition delays; Statutory clearance bottlenecks; Spares import delays (power plant); Underground mining execution risk (first in Western India); Copper and rare earths technology risk; Volatility in coal/lignite pricing; Regulatory delays in PPA pass-through
management quality / tone: Confident, long-term oriented, transparent on delays; acknowledges execution challenges but reaffirms 2030 targets; emphasizes state support, technical rigor, and patient capital; avoids overpromising on near-term volumes
non-obvious takeaways: GMDC's lignite pricing is now only 10-15% below Indonesian coal (down from 60-70% in FY21), indicating strong competitive positioning; Power plant CAPEX of Rs. 300-400cr is not a loss but a deferred investment with regulatory pass-through; Land acquisition (46% of CAPEX) is the true bottleneck, not technology or mining expertise
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GMDC's delayed lignite volume growth and power plant outage | Coal India Limited | beneficiary | Medium | GMDC's delayed supply creates incremental demand for Coal India's thermal coal in Gujarat and nearby states |
| GMDC's upcoming coal and copper supply | Adani Enterprises | loser | Low | GMDC's entry into Odisha coal may compete with Adani's captive coal-to-power model in eastern India |

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
